rows.description: A toddler wanted a biscuit and gets offered a banana. The toddler pushes it away and cries, because the goal was fixed on one thing and the request was not clear.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, delegation, trial and error

rows.description: After crying for a biscuit, a toddler sniffs, looks at the banana, and takes it. Hunger wins out, and the plan changes from getting a specific food to getting some food.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, delegation, trial and error

rows.description: A child stacks wooden blocks into a tower, watches it fall at the sixth block, and simply builds it again with the blocks in a slightly different order.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, magical thinking

rows.description: A child tells herself, "First the big blocks, then the small ones, then the flag on top," and builds in that order. The list keeps the tower's shape in mind as it grows.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, magical thinking, trial and error

rows.description: A boy sees his neighbour make a wide base with two long blocks and does the same. His tower goes higher than his earlier ones, though he cannot explain why.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, if-then plan, magical thinking, trial and error

rows.description: A child says "stay up" to the tower and insists the red block is lucky, so it goes on top. When the tower wobbles anyway, the child blames the block rather than the narrow base.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, trial and error

rows.description: After three collapses a child decides, "If it wobbles, make the bottom wider," and uses the rule on the next tower. A tested rule replaces the guess.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, magical thinking, trial and error

rows.description: The tower falls a fourth time and a child sweeps the blocks off the mat, saying "I hate this." Feelings run ahead of thinking and the learning from the earlier tries is lost.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: asking an adult, copying without fit, if-then plan, magical thinking, trial and error

rows.description: A child asks father to hold the bottom block while she stacks, then watches how he sets the blocks square. She copies his placement when she next builds alone.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, if-then plan, magical thinking, trial and error

rows.description: A child of four covers both eyes in the middle of the room and believes nobody can see. The child cannot yet take the seeker's point of view.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: copying without fit, if-then plan, magical thinking, negotiation, trial and error
